how_to_use: 1. Pull the Case and all CaseComments from Salesforce (see salesforce_queries). Read every comment; large results come back as files – read them in chunks.
2. Match the alert description and log evidence to a scenario using scenario.alert_signatures and scenario.internal_investigation.
3. Pick the template for the stage you are in: initial_response, update, approval_request, or closure.
4. Replace every {{placeholder}}. Delete optional [bracketed] text that does not apply.
5. Run the iqs_checklist before sending. After every closure, add the Resolution Details summary.

language: Never include the line 'No data disruption to backup/restore operations was observed'.
Use plain language. Explain jargon (bond0, SEL, SystemdCheck) in a few words the first time it appears.
Correct grammar and spelling on every draft. Keep closures concise.
timestamps: Only include timestamps where they add meaning (incident time, BAD/revived times, follow-up deadline).

follow_up_date.default: Two days after today at 12:00 PM UTC, written as 'Month D, YYYY, 12:00 PM UTC'.
follow_up_date.customer_gave_a_date: If the customer named a date for their work (part arrival, replacement, maintenance), set the follow-up one day after the latest date they gave.
follow_up_date.always_fill: Never leave [DATE]/[TIME] placeholders in a sent email.

customer_facing_content: Do not paste raw commands, '>>' log lines, debug output, internal insight IDs, internal Jira/engineering ticket IDs, or Slack links.
Short quoted error messages are fine when the customer needs to act on them (e.g. a tunnel connection error).
Public support.rubrik.com KB links are fine in IR 'Fix' sections.

signature.default:
Thanks and Regards,

Rohith Madineni
Customer Success Engineer – Proactive Support
Rubrik
signature.rule: If the snippet was written by another engineer, keep their name and title in the sign-off.

always_flag_to_user_before_sending: Closing earlier than a monitoring period the customer asked for.
Unanswered customer questions in the thread.
Approvals that came from a third party (e.g. an MSSP SOC) rather than the cluster owner.
Multiple nodes or multiple clusters affected at the same time (possible shared cause).
Empty or mismatched Account/contact data in Salesforce.
Truncated log output that could hide a second event.
global_rules.after_every_closure: Append 'Resolution Details:' – 1-2 plain-language lines covering the issue, the fix applied, and how it was validated / current status. No internal-only content.

every_non_closing_comment: WHAT – what was found or done.
WHEN – a concrete date/time for the next update (missing When = Reliability 0/20).
WHY – the reason for the finding or the ask.
first_three_comments: Business Impact – link the technical issue to a business consequence (or ask the customer about impact).
Technical definition signals – problem statement, context, investigation steps, environment/scope, accuracy, concrete next action, concrete timeline, rationale.

ghosted_case_signals.definition: 3 or more substantive follow-ups with no customer response.

penalties_to_avoid: Making the customer repeat information already given (-2 per instance, max -5).
Missing a promised update date (counts as a missed commitment).

comments.whereClause: ParentId IN (SELECT Id FROM Case WHERE CaseNumber = '{{case_number}}')

salesforce_queries.comments_since: Add "AND CreatedDate > YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ" to only pull new comments on a case already reviewed.
